gaps.sentence: It was careless of her — she ___ have prepared more thoroughly for the interview.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have' criticizes a failure to act properly: should have prepared.

gaps.sentence: When the lift broke, I ___ walk up ten flights of stairs.
gaps.hint: necessity created by a past event
gaps.explanation: 'Had to' expresses past necessity: had to walk.

gaps.sentence: I didn't ___ to like coffee, but now I drink it every day.
gaps.hint: negative of used to, spelled use
gaps.explanation: In the negative, 'used to' becomes 'didn't use to': use.

gaps.sentence: Sorry I am late — I ___ to take my car to the garage this morning.
gaps.explanation: Past obligation uses 'had to', since 'must' has no past form: had to.

gaps.sentence: Luckily I ___ find a parking space right outside the theatre.
gaps.hint: one particular success on that occasion
gaps.explanation: One particular success takes 'was able to': was able to find.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: If you want a refund, you ___ keep the receipt — no receipt, no refund.
gaps.hint: a necessity that applies in the future
gaps.explanation: Future necessity uses 'will have to': will have to keep.

gaps.sentence: The theatre was completely empty, so the performance ___ have been very popular.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' draws a negative conclusion from evidence: can't have been.
